short_description: Review Service Inefficiencies
description:
We have had reports from senior clinicians and exeutive team of the Trust. 

We are experiencing significant delays and inefficiencies when accessing results from EMIS Review. Each individual result can take up to a minute to load, and multiple results must often be accessed per patient. This results in excessive time spent reviewing results—up to 5–10 minutes per outpatient letter—adding 2–3 hours of admin time weekly.

We request an urgent review of the system to ensure the scalability of the system, speed of the search functionality, and improvements that can be made. Can we have guidance on the following also: increased hardware for performance, archiving results onto a different database server etc, and any other improvements to make this system more responsive in a modern age.  

This is essential to reduce clinician workload, ensure timely patient communication, and avoid inefficiencies caused by current result access methods.

If we can have something arranged soon on a call.

short_description: Suspect Folder
description:
Why are files going into the suspect folder, please could this be explained.

There are a number of files in the suspect folder at the moment and I just want an understanding to why.
close_notes:
Good morning Khaled,

Thank you for your time on the phone today, as discussed, This could be due to numerous reasons, usually reported with an error similar to: [General Fatal] Action finished due to error 'x' for some reason, and we're not sure why, something happens in Keystone that caused it to archive suspect files as it detects there an issue 

I have  thoroughly checked the log files folder, I have also checked the front end of Keystone > Monitor to find any fatal errors which could help indicate why the issue occurred, but I did not find any errors. 

This could have been caused by high usage of memory at time but it's difficult to state as the issue has been resolved and not re-occurred. It's probably worth asking IT to monitor the memory usage. I have liaised with my colleague to shed some light on the issue and they stated that were nothing obvious without the issue re-occurring and unable to find what caused the issue. 

Other reason that can cause files to go into suspect are: one of the files was really large which can cause the memory usage to run out which then throws the whole batch into suspect. Another reason is the practice names stored on keystone are too long. A few weeks back we had another trust, this was caused by Windows 'directory' constraint of 245 character limit. Where the archive location and filename has to be under 245 characters. 
 
In the below example, this directory has a total character count of XXXX, which is exceeding the Windows directory limit. 
'E:\archive\reports\discharge xml\Queenswood_Medical_Practice_(combined)\202303\02\14\report_number_1_in_dis_36756ba5-5dce-438d-bdec-3f7519f84cb5_g8333393_videofluoroscopyswallowstudyreport___4981426798_625682_XXXXX_XXXXXXXX_08091948_videofluoroscopyswallowstudyreport_21092022.pdf'

To resolve the above, it the trust shortened the practice names. 

Another reason is, the file is being looked at by another software e.g Antivirus, where it logs 'access is denied' in the Keystone log files, indicating the file is locked by another program which again will put files into suspect. 

Please do not hesitate to respond to this email if you have any questions.

Kindest Regards,

Arfan

Kind regards,
Adrian

short_description: Advice on NHS England Cyber Security Alert
description:
NHS England have sent the following Cyber Security Alert. See below and the attached email. Please can you advise if T-Quest, EMIS Review and Keystone are impacted and if so what remedial action is or has to be taken.

 
Cyber Security Vulnerability Notification

Severity: Medium
Ref: Notification of Vulnerability in electronic test requesting Interoperability system
We are writing to you from NHS England's Joint Cyber Unit because we have been made aware of a vulnerability relating to a service used in your organisation.
The interoperability mechanism that operates between the Electronic Patient Record & Request systems for Pathology and Radiology (“ordercomms”) supplied by some vendors lack important security features such as:
•	No Payload encryption or signature
•	No Access Control List to restrict origin of requests
•	Webservice Endpoint could be accessed externally through XML injection.
We have started to engage with suppliers on this issue and a number of solutions are currently or will be shortly available which will address these issues.
What can you do now?
•	Follow local risk assessment and treatment procedures.
•	Restrict endpoint access to requests from legitimate locations.
•	Prioritise investigation of any anomalous activity in Network and Endpoint logs related to Interop.
•	Make sure devices are enrolled onto Microsoft MDE capability so that the CSOC can assist in early detection.
•	Contact your suppliers of both systems to identify upgrade needs and timescales and plan for how your organisation is going to upgrade these environments.
What are the next steps?
We are expecting all vendors of the impacted systems to be releasing solutions to this issue shortly, However, due to the large marketplace providing these systems, it may be that some vendors have not been made aware of this issue by customers or NHS England. As such, we would encourage all organisations to contact their vendors to understand when they plan to fix this issue and what upgrades needs to happen in order to support a secure version of the Interop.
Should organisations have any issues with vendors providing this information or agreeing to remediate this vulnerability, you are encouraged to contact your Regional Security Lead for escalation into the Supplier Vulnerability Management process.
Handling instructions
close_notes:

close_notes:
Hello Christopher,

description:

You can see that the SNOMED codes are sent in this format separated by a comma (T01000,M72750):

OBX|3|FT|HSNM^SNOMED Code - Manual Assignment^WinPath||T01000,M72750||||||F|||20250909101100||DENTOT^Tina Denton~VAZIRR^Reza Vazir

They also appear in the interchange:

STS++SR'
FTX+RIT+++T01000,M72750'

Can you please explain why these can not be picked up in the GP's EMIS web app despite being sent in the message and how we can go about resolving this for other future things that are sent but not mapped in their system.

close_notes:
Hello Joshua,

Thanks for your message, Astha is currently on annual leave. In the meantime, I will look into matter for you. 

Other Trusts do not send SNOMED codes through the messages as they still use the read codes supplied by TRUD (NHS Technology Reference Update Distribution). They update the Read codes list with latest version supplied TRUD using below method within Keystone.

Keystone Server > Start>All Programs>Keystone Tools>Updaters>Read Code List Updater

When updating the read codes, please ensure that you turn off all the Keystone services via Monitor > from bottom right-hand corner.

We strongly advise that it is done on NPE server first so that you can test this. You will also need to do backup/restore SQL etc before updating read codes.

---

EMIS Web application can still picks up the read code from the message and then find the SNOMED which then assigns it to thecorrect SNOMED Code . 

You can login into TRUD on the Below link. If you do not have an account, you will need to register for an account.

https://isd.digital.nhs.uk/trud/user/guest/group/0/login/form

Keystone does not have any configuration for SNOMED codes, which is why it is not being picked.

close_notes:
Hello Multi,

I am pleased to update we have found/come to a resolution for your case CS1653081.

Keystone can accept the character "ö". However, when the schedule starts, this will go through a validation check and find Non-Alphanumeric Character(s). This can be turned off. However, this will cause issues with the practice system not able to view the results and future message sent via Keystone will not get checked for Non-Alphanumeric Character(s). Please note that if you decide to turn off Character Set Validation. you will not be notified of messages failing. 

To change Character Set Validation' to 'False', Navigate to:
Config > Formats > Select any of the Output e.g. 'Pathology MEDRPT v1.003 > Character Set Validation' to 'False', 

I would not recommend you turn off the Character Set Validation as this will not validate any messages sent for that selected format.

We are confident that this will resolve your issue, but if you find that this is not the case, please use the red 'Reject Solution' button so we are able to further investigate this issue for you.

short_description: Pathology 'Copy to me' Review reports
description:
Blood results requested by Primary care users through the 'copy to me' button on Review are not being correctly dated. 
THIS IS A SIGNIFICANT RISK FOR MISMANAGEMENT OF PATIENTS AND WILL IMPACT PATIENT CARE UNLESS CORRECTED.
 When bloods are originally processed, they are sent back to GPs:

*the date the specimen has been taken (in the Pathology & Radiology tree in S1, this date is recorded under the Specimen heading)
*the date the result is reported (again in the Pathology & Radiology tree in S1, this date is recorded under the Report Issued heading)
*when opening the original result you can see the date and time a clinician filed this result into the record
 

When 'copy to me' results are sent back to GPs from Review through Keystone to their SystmOne:

*there is no date reference to the date the specimen was taken (the Specimen heading is empty)
*there is a date in Report Issued (however the date under this heading is NOT the date the report was issued, but the date the result is being sent to us)
*again when opening the original result you can see the date and time a clinician filed the result (but that still doesn't show you the correct date of the test)
 
Unless this is corrected, as time moves on, 'copy to me' results will be increasingly inaccurately dated to the point that results from several months ago will appear to have been done today! Clinically this has significant implications

This is also happening for histology results.

In contrast, radiology requests though 'copy to me' are being correctly dated with the correct date of the test under the specimen heading (this is even recorded in the original report under it's own tab) and the correct Report Issued date - even though these results may be requested months after they were originally done (usually a secondary care request). So it would appear there is a way of correctly dating results, presumably this can be applied to blood results (and histology +/- microbiology)
close_notes:
Hello Mariana,

I have liaised with my colleague, Chris Hill, who has confirmed that this issue has now been resolved. He updated the rules within Keystone, including the change date and time, which resolved the issue.

We are confident this will fully address the problem; however, if you find that the issue persists, please use the red "Reject Solution" button so we can continue investigating further.

short_description: Printer settings - Enquiery
description:
STOP! Unless you are EXPECTING THIS EMAIL do NOT click on any links, or open any attachments. This may be a phishing email that could compromise our security.

Dear Team,

We are currently exploring the possibility of sharing label printers within the Trust. At present, our Sexual Health system uses Lilie connected to Zebra GX420t printers (obsolete). The recommended replacement is the Zebra ZD411.

We are examining the feasibility of sharing label printing with Cerner label printers within the Directorate. Given that we have over 100 Lilie printers, this initiative could significantly reduce NHS costs.

Both Lilie and Cerner applications are compatible with the Zebra ZD411. However, when running on a single device, the Cerner configuration is altered when running TQuest print jobs. Further investigation has revealed that Cerner's configuration requires a maximum width setting of 448.

When Lilie (TQuest) prints a label, it adjusts the print width via ZPL to either 358 or 400, depending on the label type (there are three label types). This causes issues when switching back to Cerner, as the right side of the label is cut off due to the required width of 448 being reduced to 358/400.

For more information on this known issue, please refer to the following guidance: https://supportcommunity.zebra.com/s/article/Setting-the-print-width-on-an-Z-Series-Printer?language=en_US<https://urldefense.com/v3/__https://supportcommunity.zebra.com/s/article/Setting-the-print-width-on-an-Z-Series-Printer?language=en_US__;!!IJLR5QJm7ttc!mAXVORpmgjDMC8aooULjuTyF_xAcyzwpoPjigqMb2_iVWVAWBBdFr2F6oFfWKXODkkTkY_J1vZkm4ftlattZjUuc$>

short_description: Requesting error when Sex: U
description:
Hello

Looks like there is an XML link through that is missing for the sex of U when undertaking a call from the Trust.

When a GP practice requests for a patient with sex of U it is working see example 1 attached/below, however within the Trust it fails every time with this sex.

Example 1 – working when GP Practice request

544311A

Requests and results been done by the GP Practice with a sex of Unspecified with no issue

When User at the Trust tries to request a test for the patient they get the following error – this is for all records that have this sex.

We have confirmed that the SemaHelix look up returns records with a sex of U with no issue. (see attachment for images)

 Example 2 - 069062A

Within Careflow EPR set up as Male

Within TQuest we have a number of patient records, some M and some U

When I go into Review I get these records for the patient:

Top record returns an error (see attachment)

Bottom record presents with normal form
close_notes:
Hello Jon,

Firstly, I apologise for the confusion earlier, and thank you for the additional information and examples provided.

Following further investigation with our development team, we have confirmed that the issue is related to the legacy CheckSEMA process used for Secondary Care requesting.

When an internal Trust request is made, the request passes through CheckSEMA before reaching tQuest. As part of its validation logic, CheckSEMA only accepts sex values of 'M' (Male) or 'F' (Female). Records with a sex code of 'U' (Unspecified) are therefore rejected, resulting in the following error message:

ERROR: INVALID SEX: U

This explains why requests raised from GP Practices are successful. GP Practice requests do not utilise the CheckSEMA validation process and therefore bypass this restriction, allowing patients with a sex code of 'U' to proceed to the test request page without issue.

We have discussed the possibility of amending CheckSEMA to accept 'U' as a valid value. However, CheckSEMA is a highly customised legacy component that was originally developed specifically for Shrewsbury many years ago and has remained unchanged for a significant period. Due to the age of the functionality and the potential risks associated with modifying it, no changes are currently planned.

As a result, this behaviour is considered expected based on the current CheckSEMA validation rules. For patients affected by this issue, the Trust may need to follow an alternative requesting process, such as a manual/paper request where appropriate.

As we have identified the root cause and there are currently no plans to modify the legacy CheckSEMA functionality, I will proceed with closing this case. Should you have any further questions or require any additional assistance, please do not hesitate to contact us.

Kind regards,

Arfan Mohammad
 Tech Support Specialist

close_notes:

I'm pleased to let you know that we've found a resolution for your case CS1688174.
Thank you for sharing all the details and screenshots. After reviewing everything, the reason the messages are failing validation is that the clinician has been set up with the type as Other. To resolve this, the clinician should be updated so that the Type is set to GP / Nurse / Midwife instead of Other. I've attached a screenshot showing where this needs to be changed. Once this update is made and the message is reprocessed, it will validate successfully.

Further to our recent communication 'Migration of CDS Translation Service to AWS', we have created this support ticket to assist you in connecting to our new AWS SFTP Server.
 
As part of the migration of CDS to AWS, we will require you to create a new AWS BitVise user profile to connect to the new AWS SFTP server.
 
Email: Carole.Jell@ouh.nhs.uk
 
Migration Process:
 
Phase 1: Set Up Your New Credentials
- Create your new BitVise User Profile.
- Send us your public key and externally facing IP address through this case.
- We'll process your key and confirm once it's ready.
 
Phase 2: Test Your Connection
- Connect to the new SFTP endpoint using your updated credentials.
- Confirm that everything is working as expected.
 
Action Required:
You will need to contact us via this case after completing Phase 1 so we can proceed to Phase 2.
 
Please Note:
You will now need one set of credentials per user per computer you wish to connect from.
 
Self-Service Guide:
Please refer to KB5004953 for detailed instructions on how to migrate your credentials.
 
If you have any issues or questions during the process, update this case and we will assist you.
close_notes:
Hello Carole,
I'm reaching out to provide you with an update on your case CS1702421.

As you have confirmed that no account is required, I am now in a position to resolve this ticket.

If you have any questions or need further clarification, please don't hesitate to reply to this email.

Kind regards,

Astha

short_description: CHI validation query
description:
Hi,

We have been asked to reach out to all suppliers and ask if their system makes use of CHI or more especially if it uses Validation of the CHI number. 

Modulus 10 is a check digit method used to detect errors in identification numbers. In the NHS, it’s being adopted for the CHI number when Modulus 11 options are exhausted. The algorithm sums the digits in a specific way and applies a modulo 10 operation to generate the final digit. It will only be used for new CHI numbers when Modulus 11 is unavailable, ensuring chi numbers can be registered/accepted in our Digital Systems.

Can Optum please confirm the following re Review results system:-
• Current Validation Logic
Does your system currently validate the CHI check digit?
If yes, which algorithm is used (Modulus 11, Modulus 10, or both)?
• Modulus 10 Readiness
Can your system accept and process CHI numbers with a Modulus 10 check digit?
If not, what changes are required to support Modulus 10?
• Implementation Timeline
If changes are needed, what is the estimated timeline for delivery and deployment?
Will the changes be completed by the required deadline (e.g., 01/02/2026)?
• Testing & Evidence
Will you provide test results or evidence of successful Modulus 10 validation?
• Risks & Dependencies
Are there any risks, dependencies, or support needs we should be aware of?

Thanks very much

short_description: Keystone not processing/sending messages since 13:00  after Windows Updates
description:
Hello Team,

Following windows updates and a server restart Keystone stopped processing and w have more than 3000 mesages in the queue.

Attached screnshots with errors occured. 
Could you please have a look as soon as possible.

Error Descriptions(see attahced images):
- [Fatal Event] Unable to open E:\holding\pathology\imperial\PORT7950_20251217124620415.FIL.Access denied

- [Fatal Event] This run finished due to error: 108; method: makedirectory; line: 39. Files Processed: 523 Reports Found: 523 Messages Produced: 523.

- Unable to find file: d:\keystone\dprs\sunquest_123.app for dpr: Misys Pathology 

- Unable to locate statistics DPR.
close_notes:
Hi George,

We are glad the issue is resolved now. To answer your query, there is a DPM timeout configured for 120 minutes. If a schedule in Keystone does not complete within this time, the system triggers a DPM reset, stopping the current schedule and moving files into the suspect folder. This effectively resets Keystone so it can process the next schedule. After a reset, the only thing that needs to be checked or monitored is the E:\Archive\suspect folder, as there might be files in it.
When files go into suspect, the folder will be automatically recreated. To avoid a delay in GPs receiving their reports in the future I recommend reprocessing these files yourselves if possible, which is a straight forward process:

1. Locate files in "E:\Archive\suspect"
2. Remove '.bac' extension from each of the files.
3. Copy/cut and paste files into the respective holding directory where they get processed (e.g "E:\holding\pmip")
4. Run the schedule manually from Config > Schedules if the schedule is not already due to run.
5. Delete the 'suspect' folder once all files within it have been reprocessed.

As a current workaround, other Trusts have had their IT set up email alerts to notify when a suspect folder appears in "E:\Archive" on the server, so that you can reprocess these straight away and avoid the need for constant monitoring of Keystone.

Additionally, to ensure we can assist you immediately in the future and avoid delays related to access, we kindly request that you help create accounts for our team members.Once these accounts are set up, we will be able to support you without delay.


Kind regards,
Astha

short_description: Pending requests are not appearing under the "Requests" tab
description:
Hi.

We have had a number of reports from several wards that new pathology test requests are no longer appearing under the "requests" tab. Therefore, it is not possible to view the outstanding requests for the patient.

To replicate:
1. Search for the test patient with hospital number 900000 in Review.
2. Under the "Patients" tab, click the R button to begin a new test request.
3. Enter the required details, such as full blood count, CAPNE as consultant, and A&E as location.
4. Finalise the request and accept the prompt to say printing was successful.
5. Return to Review, refresh the search, and then check under the "requests" tab. The request we have just made is not displayed.

I am not sure how this feature is supposed to work. Does the "requests" tab list every request that was ever generated, or are entries removed once all outstanding results are reported?

Could you kindly advise whether this is user error or if there is a technical problem?

Kind regards,

James
close_notes:
Hello James,

Apologies for the delay in getting back to you. I connected to the Review server and can confirm that the issue has been resolved following a reboot of the Review server.
The problem originally started on the tQuest server, where I found the following errors:

22/12/2025 04:21:58 - TQ - error in sqlSampleCommentQuery: Out of memory  
22/12/2025 04:21:58 - TQ - error in sqlSampleCommentQuery: Out of memory  
23/12/2025 00:00:09 - TQ - error in sqlSampleCommentQuery: Out of memory  
23/12/2025 00:00:09 - Out of memory  

This indicates that the code running sqlSampleCommentQuery attempted to allocate more memory than was available, resulting in an "Out of memory" error. This typically occurs when a query or the way results are fetched exceeds the memory limits of either:

The database server (e.g., SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL), or
The application/client process (e.g., a service pulling all rows into RAM).

The error was ultimately resolved by restarting the Interlink service.

Recommendation:
To help prevent similar issues in the future, I suggest your IT to monitoring memory utilisation on the tQuest server and adjusting resource limits if needed.

If you have any questions or need further clarification, please don't hesitate to reply to this email.

Kind regards,

Arfan

We need this new heading to be reflected on Review.
close_notes:
Hello Ewen,

I'm reaching out to provide you with an update on your case CS1718284.

I have discussed this with our implementation team and they have confirmed the following:-

This can be changed in the synonyms in Review for the tests. When Review imports the details for the test, it looks at the test code to see if its been seen before. If it hasn't, it uses the description from the report file itself. If it has seen that code before, it uses the description which already exists in Review, which is probably a description it originally had.

So, in those cases, the site can go into the Test Synonyms in the admin side, and edit the Display Name to be whatever they like. That will change it then for all those with that code.

If you have any questions or need further clarification, please don't hesitate to reply to this email.

Kind regards,
Adrian

short_description: copy to OBR
description: If we send a location (ODS code ) in OBR:28 will keystone send it to that location ?
close_notes:
Hello Kevin,

Apologies for the delay in getting back to you.

If a location (ODS code) is sent in OBR:28, Keystone will not route the report to that location. Keystone determines the report recipient based on the PV1 segment only.

If this is intended as a copy to recipient, the details must still be populated in the PV1 segment. For the Copy To functionality to work automatically, Keystone would need to create a duplicate message and substitute the values in PV1 with those from OBR:28. This has been confirmed as not something Keystone is able to do.

As a result, the Copy To field is informational only, it indicates who the report is for, but Keystone cannot physically route or send the report based on OBR:28.

Kindest regards,

Arfan

short_description: 'Not Delivered' correspondence
description:
We have identified a number of recent letters sent to Cornwall House Surgery (E83013) that are in 'Not Delivered' status. The most recent document appears to have sent without issue.
The error log indicates the 'message not collected by recipient after 5 days'.
Are you able to provide any further details as to why these failed please?
Thanks
close_notes:
Hello David,
 
I'm pleased to let you know that we've found a resolution for your case CS1729587.

I've reviewed all of the relevant messages, and I can confirm that everything on the Keystone side is operating correctly. The messages are being successfully sent via MESH and are reaching Arrived status as expected. After five days, any message that has not been accepted is marked as Not Delivered, which indicates that the issue occurs after the message reaches the recipient's MESH mailbox

Since Keystone has completed the sending process without any errors, and the messages are arriving at the practice's mailbox, this suggests that the problem is occurring on the recipient side. It would therefore be advisable to check with the practice to understand why the messages are not being accepted.


Kind regards,
Astha

short_description: Letters not delivered to E83049
description:
Letters sent to Langstone Way Surgery (E83049) have been failing to deliver since yesterday.
Letters are being sent via MESH, but are erroring with the following message 'unregistered to address' - are you able to clarify what that means please?
Thanks
close_notes:
Hello David,
 
I'm pleased to let you know that we've found a resolution for your case CS1730229.

I have checked the issue with letters failing to deliver to Langstone Way Surgery (E83049). The error message "unregistered to address" is occurring because the EMIS Web mailbox is missing the MESH Mail ID (attached in screenshot).

The EMIS Workflow Manager shows no mailbox configured with this MESH Mail ID, which means EMIS is unable to accept incoming letters sent via MESH. This is why deliveries are currently failing. 

I have located and confirmed the correct MESH ID in Keystone and attached this for reference.

This will need to be raised with Langstone Way Surgery to configure the mailbox with the correct MESH Mail ID. Unfortunately, the support team is not permitted to add or amend mailboxes on their behalf.


Kind Regards
Astha

close_notes:
Hello Alan,

Thank you for bringing this issue to our attention. I have investigated and can confirm that the root cause lies within Keystone.
Unfortunately, this is not something we can resolve immediately, as it requires development work. A Problem Record (PRB0051992) has been raised, and this has now been passed 

to the relevant technical team for further investigation. It will be prioritised accordingly, and a fix will be developed and released in a future version of Keystone.
Workaround in Place

A PowerShell script has been deployed on the Keystone server to recycle the suspect files back into the holding folder prior to the next run of the affected schedule.

PowerShell scripts have been placed in the following directory:
D:\EMIS_Powershell Scripts

Please inform your IT team not to modify or remove these scripts, as they are executed via Task Scheduler.
Script: Optum_Move_from_suspect_PMIP

Moves files from all child directories under
E:\archive\suspect\Telepath_PMIP_dpr_id=36
into
E:\holding\sthk_path
Deletes any empty directories within
E:\archive\suspect\Telepath_PMIP_dpr_id=36
Runs every 2 hours

I have already reprocessed the files from November and December, and these have now been successfully sent to practices.

Although your individual case will be marked as resolved, please be assured that it has been fully linked to PRB0051992. Progress updates and expected release dates for any fixes can be tracked via the Optum Help Centre using reference PRB0051992.

Kindest regards,

Arfan

description:
Keystone fatal validator: The 1st standalone test of the 1st sample has comments and/or textual results which are longer than the allowed 34650 characters,

Microbiology reports are known to contain lengthy textual comments as part of the results. These reports are issued by a referral lab and transmits into Tameside Lab LIMS Telepath (via NPEX) and reports directly to Keystone and does not pass through Trust Integration.
1. Is there a way of processing these please?
2. Please can you provide a Pathology messaging specification to Keystone

Thank you.

e.g report failure
specimen ID: M,26.1469969.XA
Partner: Medlock Vale Medical Practice
Interchange date/time: 23/02/2026  10:11:14
close_notes:
Hello Rebecca,

Following on from our MS Teams meeting, we have reviewed the error below:
[Pathology MEDRPT v1.003 Validator Fatal]"The 1st standalone test of the 1st sample has comments and/or textual results which are longer than the allowed 34,650 characters."

The 34,650?character limit is defined in the PMIP specification for Pathology. While our system can accept longer values, PMIP imposes the following constraints:

The textual result details are sent in the interchange as FTX+RIT lines.
Each FTX segment contains 5 components, each with a maximum of 70 characters (350 characters per FTX line).
A maximum of 99 FTX lines is permitted, resulting in a total capacity of 350 × 99 = 34,650 characters.

From the data reviewed, the issue is not the total number of characters, but rather the number of line breaks within the text. Each instance of a double line break creates a blank FTX line. These blank lines still count toward the 99?line limit, meaning some of the available capacity is effectively being wasted.

The blank lines will need to be removed and the message resent, which should resolve the matter.

To avoid exceeding the FTX line limit going forward, reducing unnecessary line breaks—particularly consecutive ones—will be essential.

Please do not hesitate to contact me if you have any questions or require further assistance.

I have also attached the requested specification for your reference.

Kindest regards,

Arfan

close_notes:
Hello Edwin,

The 34,650?character limit is defined by the PMIP specification for Pathology. While Keystone can technically accept more characters in the field, we are restricted by what PMIP is able to support.

Within the PMIP interchange, this limitation specifically applies to the FTX+RIT segments, which carry the textual result details.
Regarding your query about maximum line length for the T (Text) record:

Keystone itself does not impose a strict per?line limit beyond the PMIP specification; however, the overall message size is still governed by the 34,650?character maximum. If your Trust Integration Engine is failing due to long individual T?lines, it may be due to how the receiving system handles line wrapping or segmentation rather than a Keystone limitation.

If helpful, we can review an example of a failing message to confirm whether the issue is related to PMIP constraints or line?handling within your interface engine.

Kind regards,

Arfan

short_description: Radiology (FIL) formats
description: We are wondering at what point a Radiology Report that is compiled by our Radiology Imaging System (RIS) and then is passed onto our Electronic Patient Record System and finally proceeding to the Keystone Holding folder (hss_radiology) does it become a FIL file. Does Keystone convert the report into a "port5990_xxxxxxxx.fil" - This will assist with our Radiology UAT with Keystone 1.8. Thank you.
close_notes:
Hello Ian,

The Radiology report becomes a .FIL file at the point it is received and processed by the Keystone port listener, not during the earlier RIS or EPR stages.

When a message is received on the configured port (e.g. 5990), the process is as follows:

1. The incoming HL7 message is written to a temporary file in E:\temp\

2. Once the transaction completes successfully, the file is renamed and moved into the Keystone holding directory: E:\holding\hss_radiology\

3. At this point, Keystone converts the file to the format port5990_XXXXXXXXXXXXXXX.fil, and it is then available for Keystone to process.

Below is a snippet from the port listener log showing an example of an ORU^R01 message being received, temporarily stored, and then moved into the holding folder as a .fil file:

09/04/2026 07:45:48 - port 5990 Start of transaction, received
09/04/2026 07:45:48 - port 5990 write to temporary file: e:\temp\port5990_000004DB.tmp
09/04/2026 07:45:48 - port 5990 msg type: ORU^R01
09/04/2026 07:45:48 - port 5990 End of transaction, received
09/04/2026 07:45:48 - port 5990 Rename temporary file:
E:\temp\port5990_000004DB.tmp to
E:\holding\hss_radiology\port5990_20260409074548714.fil

This indicates the exact point at which the report becomes a .fil file for Keystone 1.8, which should assist with your Radiology UAT activities.

Please do not hesitate to contact me if you have any questions or need further clarification.

Kindest regards,

Arfan

My understanding is that that these are all true duplicates.

The following question, however, has been raised by a colleague: if a report is issued, but while waiting in the queue to be processed in Keystone, the report is amended in the LIMS and sent again, which will be under the same report ID (?), so there are two separate messages under the same report ID awaiting processing. My belief is that in this circumstance, the messages  would get separate interchange IDs and so the issue of DTS error / duplicates would not arise. Please could you therefore confirm that duplicates due to interchange number being already received can be safely processed / removed from the list.

close_notes:
Hello Ian,

Thank you for your time on the phone today. As discussed, when a duplicate interchange issue occurs, an error will be logged on the front end of Keystone stating "Unable to run DTSLink error." I can confirm that when this issue occurs, it does not alter the interchange content or its values, and the exact same interchange is sent again to the practice.

A Problem Record (PRB) has been raised under reference PRB0052462 for this issue, and it will now be passed to the relevant technical department for further investigation.

In the meantime, the current workaround is for the Trust to reboot the Keystone Application Server on a regular basis, as this is the only temporary fix available.

Although your individual case will be marked as resolved, please be reassured that it has been linked to PRB0052462. You can track the progress and expected release dates of any fixes on the Optum Help Centre:
https://www.optumhelpcentre.co.uk/csm (reference: PRB0052462).

We're sorry that we aren't able to provide an immediate fix on this occasion. We appreciate your patience while this is reviewed by our technical teams and a permanent resolution is developed.

Hi Ben,

Uninstalling update KB5087537 has temporarily resolved the issue. However, based on the information available, this update is known to introduce issues affecting domain controller lookup and DNS-related functionality in certain scenarios—particularly in Windows Server 2016 environments.

From the information gathered, this appears to be linked to a known issue introduced by this update. Specifically, after installing the update, domain controller discovery may fail on Windows Server 2016 systems when the server hostname is 15 characters long. In these cases, DCLocator calls (for example, using nltest /dsgetdc:<domain> /pdc) can return ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER, preventing applications and administrative tools from locating a domain controller.

This can also impact scenarios that rely on domain controller lookup, such as DNS resolution and DFS Namespace access, which aligns with the behaviour observed in your environment.

At present, Microsoft has acknowledged this as a known issue and is investigating, but no fix or timeline has been provided yet. Given this, the recommended approach is to not reinstall KB5087537 at this time and instead wait for a future Windows security update that addresses this issue.

https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/5890529/kb5087537-breaks-dfs-namespace-on-windows-server-2

I have spoken about this case with Chris Hill, OCM Implementation specialist, who was part of the OCM Implementation Team that carried out upgrade work on NCA Review system over three months ago with your move from Labcentre to WinPath.

He informed me that the "Preferred import date" in the Winpath Translation Processing Options section, which has 3 options to pick from - see NCA_OCS_WinPath_Pref_Imp_Date.png, is configured for "Sample receipt date", see NCA_OCS_WinPath_Proc_Opt.png

This was set during upgrade work on NCA Review system over three months ago with your move from Labcentre to WinPath this because it mirrors their Labcentre action, which they were using prior to WinPath, so when we setup the new action for Winpath, we mirrored the same import settings. This was the agreed configuration during UAT testing of this upgrade which was fully signed-off as working correctly.

So I believe that means that where it shows the "Imported date/time" in Review, that is actually the "Sample receipt date", not the actual date the report was imported into Review.

This setting can be changed to "Date of Import" instead, as above, but it will affect ALL Pathology being imported, not just Histopathology. This will have to be discussed internally with ALL affected teams for the differing pathology types, etc., as this is setting itself mirrors the same as what it did before in Labcentre.

The above placeholder which is used to determine which field in the HL7 will be imported \ assigned to whatever within the Review GUI is detailed below:

OBR.6 = %RECDATE% --> Sample Receipt Date

short_description: CrowdStrike Falcon possibly causing 1705 errors due to file locks?
description: We have had a number of failures in the generation of messages in Keystone. Files Have fallen into the suspects folder. These have been resubmitted and have been fine. The error we are seeing in the logs is 1705. The Trust has recently switched AV to Counterstrike Falcon and this is running on the Keystone server snt-emisks-v01.xspttrust.nhs.uk. Would it be possible to get some concrete evidence that the errors tha we are seeing are due to AV file locks?
close_notes:
Hello Nicholas,

Thank you for the update.

Based on the information provided, we cannot conclusively confirm that CrowdStrike Falcon is the cause of the 1705 – File access is denied errors.

Whilst antivirus software can sometimes cause file locking issues, the error itself only indicates that Keystone was unable to access the file at the required time. Unfortunately, the Keystone log files do not capture details of the process or application that has locked or interacted with the file, so we are unable to provide definitive evidence that CrowdStrike Falcon is responsible.

As the issue persists following the CrowdStrike sensor update and server reboot, it is possible that another third-party application or service installed on the server is interacting with the processing folders and causing the conflict. This could include security software, backup agents, monitoring tools, file indexing services, or other applications with file system access.

Unfortunately, from the Keystone logs alone, we cannot determine which specific process is causing the file lock. We would therefore recommend that your IT team investigate the server further, reviewing any software that may be monitoring or accessing the Keystone processing directories. They may wish to use OS-level monitoring tools to identify which process is locking the affected files when the issue occurs.

Please let us know if any additional evidence is identified during your investigation, and we will be happy to review it with you.

Kind regards,
Arfan Mohammad
Tech Support Specialist

short_description: Keystone issue
description:
Hi Support, on Friday (19/6) morning we had an issue with our keystone where the daily housekeeping task appeared stuck and no results had been sent out.  I had cancelled the task and restarted keystone in order to get our results processing.  It has become evident that our results were building in the background.  Whilst the initial sets of results were sent out after the restart - more results had built up during the processing time and then eventually keystone could not process the files.

Is it possible to look retrospectively to see what had/could've caused the housekeeping task to be stuck or appear stuck?
close_notes:
Hello Mark,

I am pleased to update you that we have found a resolution for your case CS1802899.

The schedules themselves ran successfully; however, I agree that the Housekeeper (Butler) process took longer than expected to complete.

Having reviewed the logs and discussed this with Peter Moran, I can confirm that the PowerShell housekeeping scripts are operating correctly. These scripts run externally to Keystone and there is no indication that they contributed to the issue.

The process that appears to have caused the delay was the Butler Housekeeper, which is a separate automated housekeeping component that is hard-coded within the Keystone backend. From the logs, the Butler process exceeded its usual runtime while the system was working through a high volume of messages and housekeeping tasks.

Although Keystone showed the housekeeping schedule as active from 1:00am, the logs indicate that the Butler process completed at approximately 09:32am, with a total runtime of 23 minutes and 6 seconds for that execution. During this period, the system was also processing a large volume of messages, which resulted in additional messages accumulating and subsequently increasing the backlog experienced over the weekend.

Once the volume of outstanding messages had reduced and Keystone resumed normal processing, the Butler housekeeping process was able to catch up. Since then, we have not identified any further occurrences of this issue.

Please see the attached screenshots from the logs which show the relevant housekeeping activity and completion times.

We are confident that this will resolve your issue. However, if you find that this is not the case, please use the red 'Reject Solution' button so that we are able to further investigate this issue for you.

short_description: DPM reset and indexing very slow, users complaining
description:
Check indexing or possibly disk. Something is slowing down..? DPM reset is red, I think last time it was to do with housekeeper task failing

rdeluca@nhs.net.
close_notes:
Hello Robert,

I have investigated this further and have not found any errors within the HouseKeeper logs that would indicate the housekeeping task became stuck or failed.

I also reviewed the database logs and can see that the housekeeping process was completing successfully. However, some housekeeping runs were taking significantly longer than normal due to the volume of data that had accumulated prior to the DPM reset on 23/07/2026.

Based on the information available, it appears that the task was still processing rather than being stuck. The increased runtime is consistent with a larger-than-usual backlog of data being processed, which would explain why results continued to build up and why the process may have appeared unresponsive. This would also explain why the DPM Inactivity Monitor triggered a reset at 04:00:24 on 23/07/2026, as shown in the attached screenshot.

I have attached screenshots from both the database logs and the Keystone maintenance registry settings for reference. The database logs show that the housekeeping tasks continued to start and complete successfully during this period, with no evidence of task failures. The DPM timeout is configured for 60 minutes, and the reset appears to have been triggered as a result of extended processing activity rather than an application issue.

At this stage, I have not found any evidence of an application error, failed housekeeping task, or process deadlock. The behaviour observed appears to be consistent with the system processing a larger-than-normal workload, which resulted in longer execution times and ultimately caused the DPM inactivity monitor to perform a reset.

As such, no further action is required from the Keystone perspective at this time.

Please let me know if you would like me to investigate anything further.

Kind regards,

Arfan Mohammad

short_description: Not Acknowledged Reports - Non-Alpha Numeric Characters
description:
There is an issue with Keystone sending Non-Alpha Numerical characters in reports to GP surgeries which has seen a major uplift recently, especially in Cellular Pathology Reports.  These are commonly ASCII 160 Non-Breaking Space which then casue the report to be rejected by the GP system (EMIS Web). Is there any possibility that these characters can be stripped from the reports on the Keystone side or the EMIS Web side? 

We understand that there are other characters in reports that cause these issues too like ASCII code 215 (multiplication sign) or ASCII code 198 (squared sign) but given the clinical significance of these, we would have to change our processes to strip these ASCII codes manually. 

Over the past year we have had 50+ reports with this issue, as opposed to 5-10 a year previous to this.
